miejsce: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
streszczenie: This repository contains the corrected reproducibility package accompanying the study Polish Legal Language between Interpretability and Prediction: A Stylometric and Machine-Learning Study. The study examines linguistic variation across 120 Polish statutes representing six legal domains: administrative law, civil law, criminal law, economic law, labour and social-security law, and tax and financial law. The balanced corpus contains 20 acts per domain and 591 cleaned text segments, covering legislation published between 1997 and 2024. The analytical design combines corpus-based stylometry, legal phraseology, content masking, principal component analysis, inferential statistics, and supervised machine learning. Four language representations are compared: full-text TF-IDF with a linear SVM, content-masked TF-IDF with a linear SVM, 83 explicit stylometric features with logistic regression, and 83 stylometric features supplemented by 19 nonredundant legal-phraseology indicators. A separate year-only baseline is used to control for chronological information. The package includes: Python and Google Colab analysis code; corpus and segment metadata; corrected act-level and segment-level stylometric features; content-masked text representations; feature-audit results; fold-level and summary model-performance tables; out-of-fold predictions; class-level precision, recall, and F1 scores; Kruskal–Wallis and post-hoc Mann–Whitney U results with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction; PCA coord

tytul_openalex: Replication data for: Payment Size, Negative Equity, and Mortgage Default
miejsce: ICPSR Data Holdings
streszczenie: This paper studies the treatment effect of monthly payment size on mortgage default, using a sample of adjustable-rate loans that experienced large payment reductions thanks to the recent low interest rate environment. Payment size has an economically large effect on repayment behavior; for instance, cutting the required payment in half reduces the delinquency hazard by about 55 percent. Importantly, the link between payment size and delinquency is equally strong for borrowers that are significantly underwater on their mortgage. Relying on payment reductions for identification circumvents the selection concerns due to prepayments that would be associated with rate increases.

For each corpus, participants were provided with pairwise authenticity labels (authentic vs. imitation/falsification) and, where applicable, finer-grained group identities corresponding to individual scribes, forgers, or manuscript sources. streszczenie: Artificial intelligence (AI) disclosure in advertising may carry risks for consumers' brand attitudes. Drawing on 101,623 YouTube comments and two experiments (N = 129 each), this research examines whether, why, and under what conditions AI disclosure negatively affects brand attitudes. Study 1 analyzes comments on advertisements that 12 brands published between January 1, 2024, and November 5, 2026. Large language model-based sentiment evaluations, validated against annotations from two independent human annotators, reveal significant negative associations between brand-authored AI disclosure and sentiment directed toward the brand, controlling for other covariates, including brand fixed effects, with advertisement-clustered standard errors. Two experiments featuring hypothetical brands' advertisements on Instagram and their own websites, respectively, demonstrate that AI disclosure negatively affects brand attitudes, with the effect weakening as product involvement increases. Moreover, a moderated serial mediation relationship suggests that AI disclosure reduces perceived advertising effort, which in turn undermines advertisement credibility and, ultimately, brand attitudes, with negative indirect effects becoming stronger as product involvement decreases. In Study 3, the negative effect remained even when AI was described as creating advertising text based on human reviews. tytul_w_rejestrze: Nodding of virtual humans does not increase customer trust: a temporal analysis.
tytul_openalex: Nodding of virtual humans does not increase customer trust: a temporal analysis.
miejsce: Radboud Repository (Radboud University)
streszczenie: This repository is the data storage of the study: "Nodding of virtual humans does not increase customer trust: a temporal analysis". This study aimed to research how nodding of virtual humans influences trust, using mediation analysis and studying temporal dynamics of trust within an interaction. It was an online experiment (N = 429), using a between-subjects design with two conditions: a virtual human either nodded during listening or did not. To isolate nodding optimally, participants watched a video of a customer interaction: a virtual human advised a customer on a wardrobe. While watching, participants used a slider scale to keep updating their temporal trust in the virtual human. Afterwards, participants answered questionnaires on trust and perceived responsiveness. This repository contains the anonymized participant data of the study including both the raw and cleaned data, and a codebook for the datafiles. It contains the R file used to analyze the cleaned data, and materials of the study, such as: scenario, Qualtrics questionnaire, the interaction videos used for manipulation. There is also a document that explains the code behind the temporal trust scale. A description of all files can be found in the readme file.

The dataset contains 107 acoustic features extracted from 2327 Polish speech utterances from the nEMO corpus. The recordings represent three affective classes: sad, neutral, and happiness. The data were prepared for research on speech emotion recognition under speaker-independent evaluation conditions, especially leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) validation. Each row in the main CSV file corresponds to one utterance. The dataset includes speaker identifiers, utterance identifiers, emotion labels, class IDs, source file names, and 107 numeric acoustic descriptors. The acoustic features cover prosodic, phonatory, temporal, energy-related, spectral, and cepstral properties of speech, including F0 statistics, jitter, shimmer, harmonic-to-noise ratio, pause and onset measures, RMS energy, zero crossing rate, spectral centroid, bandwidth, rolloff, flatness, MFCCs, and delta MFCCs. The release is intended to support reproducibility of the feature-based analyses reported in the article and to enable further research on Polish speech emotion recognition, speaker-independent affect classification, acoustic feature analysis, and comparison of classical acoustic descriptors with deep learning approaches such as wav2vec 2.0 and WavLM. miejsce: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
streszczenie: DeepLips is a labelled Portuguese audio-visual speech dataset comprising 270 synchronized video recordings from 27 adult speakers, with 10 prompted utterances per participant. Recordings were captured using a Blackview BV9800 Pro smartphone at 1280 × 720 resolution and 30 fps, with synchronized audio, in a controlled frontal setup approximately 1 metre from the participant, using a homogeneous blue background and artificial lighting. Each video is paired with a manually produced word-level .align file containing temporal boundaries for the five spoken tokens as well as initial and final silence. The dataset is intended for research in visual speech recognition, lipreading, audio-visual alignment, multimodal speech processing, transfer learning, and speaker-independent evaluation.

streszczenie: Description The Klarna Product Page Dataset is a dataset of publicly available pages corresponding to products sold online on various e-commerce websites. The dataset contains offline snapshots of 51,701 product pages collected from 8,175 distinct merchants across 8 different markets (US, GB, SE, NL, FI, NO, DE, AT) between 2018 and 2019. On each page, analysts labelled 5 elements of interest: the price of the product, its image, its name and the add-to-cart and go-to-cart buttons (if found). These labels are present in the HTML code as an attribute called klarna-ai-label taking one of the values: Price, Name, Main picture, Add to cart and Cart. The snapshots are available in 3 formats: as MHTML files (~24GB), as WebTraversalLibrary (WTL) snapshots (~7.4GB), and as screeshots (~8.9GB). The MHTML format is less lossy, a browser can render these pages though any Javascript on the page is lost. The WTL snapshots are produced by loading the MHTML pages into a chromium-based browser. To keep the WTL dataset compact, the screenshots of the rendered MTHML are provided separately; here we provide the HTML of the rendered DOM tree and additional page and element metadata with rendering information (bounding boxes of elements, font sizes etc.). The folder structure of the screenshot dataset is identical to the one the WTL dataset and can be used to complete the WTL snapshots with image information.
